commenti.body:
Most of the films you mentioned were books before they became film, and being philosophical in sci-fi literature is far more intrinsic to the medium than it is to film, so it isn't that tied to film at all, I'd say. 

Pretty much the opposite.

As far as recommendations go, I think *Alphaville* really hits what you're describing, as does *World on a Wire*, probably.

Most of Cronenberg's films also hit this to various degrees. If I'm reading you correctly, I think *Scanners* and *The Brood* fit the bill the most by being extremely grounded and un-futuristc for the most part.

*a Scanner Darkly*, book and movie is also very light on the tech and futurism.

*Primer* may fit your bill, it is certainly sci-fi, and certainly philosophical and low-fi, but maybe not in the ways you are looking for, same can be said for *Under the Skin* and *Man Who Fell to Earth,* and *Quiet Earth*

Science is an aspect of philosophy, and philosophy is an aspect of religion. Fiction is the same as religion. Therefore, "science fiction" combines science with religion, without the intermediary of philosophy. So, if you add philosophy to that, it has all three. That's definitely the best kind of film. I think Solaris is a good example

I really liked Vanilla Sky and Solaris (2003 I think. The one with George Clooney.) Both american remakes of foreign films, but both better than the originals. Who the hell wants to read subtitles? That's why I go to the movies, so I don't have to read!

The film that immediately came to my mind is Claire Denis' *High Life*.  That is precisely what you are looking for.

Sci-Phi is an interesting term for the sub genre, although arguably borders on the pretentious. Good science fiction is often philosophical, either directly in the text or the material is thought-provoking. I like the layperson term "heady sci-fi" better, but maybe that is pretentious too.

"the man from Earth" 2007. Nothing to wild and exciting but a well done philosophical soft sci-fi.

I love me some independence day and other action packed SciFi. But there's something about man from earth that is just cozy

In addition to the ones already recommended, I would also mention After Yang, Dead Man's Letters, Last and First Men (technically a movie but moreso a reading of the novel, hard to explain) and Aniara. Haven't seen A Visitor to a Museum yet but it has a high chance of fitting this criteria based on the vibe I'm getting from it. A lot of the best scifi is adapted from novels of the past century, and so many soviet bloc ones specifically! But maybe I am biased towards them.

Hard to Be God is a wasted opportunity. German went too far with his style, it's barely watchable. The book is pretty straightforward and raises just enough questions to make a movie interesting and engaging.

You are correct, but to me Roadside Picnic doesn't feel like Stalker. It goes into more detail as to the effects of the zone and the cause of it. In fact I think I wasn't clear of what the zone was supposed to be until I read the book.

World on a Wire absolutely fits the bill, I forgot about that one. I will check out Alphaville

> Good science fiction is often philosophical

This is true, some TNG episodes for example are very philosophical. However it's so evidently and visually sci-fi. In the films I mentioned you could be dropped at many scenes without context and not know it's sci-fi at all, or confuse it with fantasy.

One of my favorite literary genres is sci-fantasy, where the division between sci-fi and fantasy is not very clear. I think it's the ambiguity of text that allows this, and I'm not sure if there's examples of successfully pulling this off in film.
I've seen that a long time ago, I agree it fits the bill but, while it's worthwhile, the movies I listed excel so much in the cinematography I feel off about putting it on the same tier.
I have Last and First Men on my computer, that's going at the top of the queue, thanks!
I had a dizzying and awe inspiring experience when I watched it, although I can definitely agree he "went too far", but I found it extremely interesting without knowing anything about the book.
Did you understand what was going on the screen?
Yeah and I was in a constant state of fascination as to how they pulled this off, or came up with some of the shots. It's truly like no other film I've ever seen and that's high praise in my eyes.
